title: slim credential orchestrator, session smoother, and stream ergonomic RX
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: multiple SDKs have accumulated ad-hoc credential prefetch and retry logic that complicates onboarding and leads to subtle stream resumptions differences between Python/TS/Go. This PR introduces a lightweight, language-agnostic credential orchestrator shape plus a session smoother primitive to reduce jitter during token handoffs and to make stream cancellation/resume behavior more predictable.

Motivation: reduce cross-language parity gaps that surface as intermittent reauth races and noisy telemetry, and provide a single ergonomic surface for SDK authors to opt into prefetch, lease windows, and bounded backoff profiles.

Summary of changes:
- Add "credential orchestrator" API surface and reference implementations in sdk-python, sdk-typescript, sdk-go. The orchestrator exposes: lease_hint, prefetch_margin, and a small callback interface for token renewal events.
- Introduce SessionSmoother (library-level primitive) that tracks recent heartbeat/retry outcomes and adapts cooldowns to avoid thrashing on intermittent KMS latency spikes.
- Standardize a compact retry profile (named "balanced-light") across SDKs and wire it into streaming helpers so streaming clients get consistent backoff/telemetry.
- Surface opt-in streaming telemetry hooks (stream_start_id, resumptions_count, last_lease_age) to help correlate reauth events with server-side logs.
- Small ergonomic wrappers: async iterator helpers in Python, generator variants in TypeScript, context-friendly session factory in Go.

Design notes: the orchestrator is intentionally minimal: it does not change existing auth protocols (no new tokens exchanged), it schedules background renewals and publishes lease events. Integration hooks are pluggable so higher-level apps (console/observability) can register to receive synthetic events.

Checklist:
- [x] API sketches reviewed with SDK leads (Evan/Priya)
- [x] Unit tests for orchestrator state machine in all three SDKs
- [x] Compatibility e2e against staging gateway (stream resume + token rotation)
- [x] Telemetry schema bump reviewed with observability team
- [x] Docs draft for SDK migration/examples

Tests and validation: CI runs full tri-language unit matrix and cross-SDK golden e2e (stream resume scenarios). One flaky test (ts/stream/resume-timing) rerun during review; final CI green after increased test timeout and a small harness fix.

Observability: added three new trace fields and two metrics (cred_orchestrator_renew_attempts, session_smoother_cooldowns) and updated the schema version.

Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag and staged rollout to hosted customers via console toggles; default remains off for Dedicated/Private until we complete a short compatibility window.

Backwards compatibility: this is non-breaking; SDKs add new helpers but preserve old auth paths.

Migration docs: added examples in each SDK showing recommended usage for streaming consumers.

Impact: reduces observed reauth-induced stream resets by ~62% in internal canary traffic (measured over a 48h window) and normalizes retry counts across languages.
commits: init: add orchestrator interface and python reference impl
ts: generator + hook bindings + telemetry shim
go: session factory + context helpers + small conn-dedup layer
sdk-common: define retry profile 'balanced-light' and telemetry schema bump
tests: tri-lang e2e harness updates and flaky test timeout adjustments
review_thread: Priya Nair: Can we avoid a background goroutine per client in Go? Suggest centralizing renewal into the connection pool.
Maya Chen: Addressed — refactored go orchestrator to use a pool-backed renewal worker, added comment and unit test.
Diego Rivera: Telemetry fields look good; please sanitize IDs (no PII). Also add an integration test for lease expiry edge-case.
Maya Chen: Added sanitizer and integration test exercising lease expiry race; updated observability schema notes.
Evan Park: Approve after resolving flaky TS test and documenting behavior when orchestrator is disabled (fallback to legacy path).
CI Bot: ts/stream/resume-timing failed on first run (timeout), rerun -> passed. All checks green.
notes_on_backwards_compatibility: No breaking changes. All SDKs keep the legacy token fetch path; orchestrator is opt-in. Migration notes included in docs and examples.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in Credential Orchestrator and SessionSmoother in Python/TypeScript/Go; adds 'balanced-light' retry profile and new streaming telemetry hooks. Improves stream stability and cross-SDK parity for auth/retry behavior.
